text:
sasha: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — thinking out loud about adding a lightweight workload-driven sampling pass before heavy benching. Main goal: catch obvious regressions fast without burning bench credits.
liam: love the idea. do you mean something like a 1-2s microbench that exercises kv cache & batch logic? :thinking_face:
sasha: yeah, microbench ~200 short traces + 50 long traces. not exact numbers, but small enough to be cheap and fast. catch OOMs, shape mismatches, big latency degradations.
maya: we should also validate tokenizer mapping and prompt templates in the same pass. last month a model had a changed bos token and broke many prompts.
sasha: good call. include a token-sanity check + inference smoke producing top-k logits for a small seed set. if tokenizer mismatch -> fail fast.
jin: how do we define "fail fast"? block admission or just flag and require manual signoff? for Dedicated customers blocking would be scary.
liam: propose policy: for hosted/non-prod accept with warnings; for Dedicated/Private if microbench fails hard (OOM, severe error) -> block. Token mismatch -> block for any production tier.
sasha: +1. also need fallback routing: if a model passes microbench but later runtime shows odd tail latencies, route to compatible variant (quantized or smaller) automatically. that's longer-term but related.
maya: implementation detail: where does the microbench live? inside the ingest worker or separate job?
jin: prefer separate job to avoid slowing ingestion path. ingest worker should enqueue model for microbench, then bench coordinator picks up. microbench result should be in registry metadata.
liam: agreed. metadata keys: microbench.status=(pass/warn/fail), microbench.metrics=(p95,p99,mem_peak,token_misrate), microbench.report_url. keep simple strings.
sasha: example microbench CLI we sketched:
```
bench-smoke --model-id $MID --samples 250 --seqs 32 --output json --token-sanity true
```
put outputs in GCS and attach link.
maya: can we reuse existing bench harness? lightweight runner needs to skip expensive eval suites and quantization tests. just runtime perf + token checks.
jin: yes, add a --fast flag to harness. important to limit GPU hours. also we should gate how many concurrent microbenches per region.
liam: ops note: add rate limiter in intake to avoid spikes during large model directories being uploaded. maybe a token bucket per org.
sasha: risk: false negatives where microbench passes but a full bench later reveals issues. we'll need a decayed confidence score and require periodic full bench for models hitting traffic thresholds.
maya: suggest automatic promotion: start in "soft-serve" with traffic cap 1% until full bench completes. that buys safety.
jin: sounds good. can we wire this into rollout config: {"initial_traffic":0.01, "microbench_required":true, "fullbench_deadline":"7d"}? small JSON blob in registry.
liam: minor: ensure telemetry IDs propagate so bench traces can be linked to request ids for replay. else we lose context.
sasha: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with these concrete fields, example CLI, and gating matrix (hosted vs dedicated). will ping @maya and @jin for review.
onboard-bot: scheduled job created: microbench-coordinator will pick up queued models every 5m. more details: https://internal.redwood/ops/microbench
sasha: cool, thanks all. I'll start doc and open a PR for the harness change. :rocket:
